$comment: Example Jarvis catalog. Copy, adjust paths, then: jarvis start --catalog catalog.json

defaults.$comment_max_in_flight: worker turns in flight FLEET-WIDE, and the only cap here that is not per project: max_concurrent rations a project, this rations the ACCOUNT, which is what runs out when several projects dispatch at once. Whichever is tighter binds. Held-back orders wait as pending; nothing fails. No per-project override — a project cannot own a share of a shared window
defaults.$comment_autocompact: how large a worker's conversation may grow before Claude Code compacts it (claude --autocompact). Every API call re-reads the whole conversation, so this multiplies into the bill on every call; 100000-1000000, or null for the model's own window

os.$comment_cold_prefix_floor: cost reporting only, never worker behaviour: the cache read below which a cold turn boundary kept NOTHING and so was the cache entry EXPIRING, rather than the prompt prefix moving (which no cache TTL can help). Set it just under the smallest static system-prompt head across your projects — roughly a CLAUDE.md plus the worker briefing. There is NO fallback: with no catalog registered, jarvis cost fails rather than guessing. cold_prefix_floor_max is the guard rail on it, raise both together. See docs/superpowers/findings/2026-08-30-where-the-800-dollars-went.md
os.$comment_knowledge: worker prompts get an INDEX of the knowledge base and fetch entries on demand; inject_limit caps the entries pinned in verbatim

neo.$comment: Neo answers worker questions on your behalf; review its answers in the UI's neo tab
neo.$comment_digest: which model shortens an over-long question for the neo tab; "" turns it off and every question renders in full

worker.$comment: inherits os.defaults.permission_mode (auto); override here to restrict a project
worker.append_system_prompt: Run the test suite before opening any PR.

$comment: Privileged actions a worker may ATTEMPT, with an independent review by Neo
deciding whether they run. Omit this key entirely (the default) and workers
simply cannot do these things. Known gates: pr_merge, release,
IMPORTANT: do not ALSO list a gated command under permissions.deny. Claude
Code evaluates deny rules regardless of what a hook returns, so the deny wins
and the approved retry is blocked too — silently. `jarvis doctor` reports this
